title: “A Richly Deserved Reward”: Carlos Alcaraz Hails Alexander Zverev as German Nears World No. 1
text:
Alcaraz on Zverev’s No. 1: ‘He Totally Deserves It’

 “A Richly Deserved Reward”: Carlos Alcaraz Hails Alexander Zverev as German Nears World No. 1 
 ATP Tour “A Richly Deserved Reward”: Carlos Alcaraz Hails Alexander Zverev as German Nears World No. 1 
 Jim Flannigan | 27 October 2026 | 3 min read Carlos Alcaraz at the Vienna Open Press Confrence - Photo: IMAGO/Branislav Racko Share this article
 Add us as a preferred source on Google 
 Carlos Alcaraz has praised Alexander Zverev as the German closes in on the world No. 1 ranking, calling it “a richly deserved reward” for his consistency and physical strength. Speaking in Vienna, the Spaniard also admitted he misses his battles with Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic.
 Alcaraz, playing in Vienna for the first time since 2021, was asked about Zverev’s remarkable season at his press conference on Monday. “He totally deserves it,” Alcaraz said. “Tennis isn’t just about stepping onto the court and playing well. It’s not enough to be the best in one particular match: what really matters is the consistency you show throughout the entire season.”
 “In Sascha’s Case, He Has Both”
 The world No. 3 highlighted the combination of skill and physical resilience that has taken Zverev to the top. “Some players stand out through their style or level of play, while others shine through their physical attributes. In Sascha’s case, I think he has both,” he said.
 He singled out Zverev’s ability to compete week after week without breaking down. “He has an extraordinary level of play and the physical qualities that allow him to compete all year long, reach finals week after week, avoid major injuries, and stay consistent without wearing down too much,” Alcaraz said.
 “That’s why I think he fully deserves to be No. 1 and that he has had an exceptional season. I’m very happy for him, because I know how hard he worked to achieve this goal. It’s a richly deserved reward.”
 Two Wins From the Top
 Zverev has already secured the year-end No. 1 ranking, which he clinched on October 12 after Alcaraz lost in Shanghai. The only question is when he will officially take over from Sinner, who ended his season early with a knee injury.
 According to the ATP, the German will become world No. 1 on November 2 if he reaches the quarterfinals in Vienna, where he is the top seed. He opens against Spanish wild card Martín Landaluce.
 The 29-year-old will become only the second German man to reach No. 1, after Boris Becker in 1991, and the 30th player in the history of the ranking. He has earned it with the best season of his career, winning his first major at Roland Garros in June, reaching the Wimbledon final and then winning the US Open in September.
 “I Miss Those Battles”
 Alcaraz also reflected on the lack of matches against his biggest rivals in 2026. He has not faced Sinner since losing to him in the Monte-Carlo final in April, and his last meeting with Djokovic came in January, when he beat the Serb in the Australian Open final to win his first title in Melbourne.
 “Facing these players demands something different. When you play against them, you understand what you need to work on in your next practice session,” he said. “These are matches that push you to your limits and help you identify the areas where you need to improve.”
 “I miss those battles, as well as watching those matches from the outside. I think playing them again will be very important for me.”
 He may not have to wait long. All three are expected at the Six Kings Slam exhibition in Riyadh in late December, where Sinner returns from injury. Before that, Alcaraz faces Karen Khachanov in his first-round match in Vienna as he chases a fourth title of the season.
